units: Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵇ top (ref. to Ps. LVIII, 6) [read:] כל מי שהיה חוֹבְרוֹ הוא חוברו whoever assisted him (in his political ambition), him he befriended.—Esp. חוֹבֵר, pl. חוֹבְרִים, חוֹבְרִין having a share in the ownership of a sacrifice, v. חֲבוּרָה.

<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 9:9">Men. IX, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Menachot 93b:20">93ᵇ</cite> bot.) <he>אחד מניף לכל החו׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>חֲבֵרִים</he>) one of the company does the waving in behalf of all of them. Ib. 94ᵃ <he>נתמעטה בחו׳</he> is reduced in numbers as regards the participants (only one of them being required to act).
<cite ref="Temurah 2a">Tem. 2ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Arakhin 2a:34">Arakh. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>בעלי ח׳</he> (sub. <he>קרבן</he>) partners of a sacrifice (also <he>בעלי קרבן</he>).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 11a:3">B. Bath. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>חָבְרוּ עליו וכ׳</he> his brothers &c. combined to protest against his actions.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:31">Lam. R. to I, 5</cite> <he>מביאין חוֹבֵר וחוֹבְרִין וכ׳</he> they procure a charmer and charm the serpent.

<cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 172:1">Sifré Deut. 172</cite> <he>ה׳ מרובה</he> he who charms large objects; <cite ref="Keritot 3b:97">Ker. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>ח׳ גדול</he>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 65a:21">Snh. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>חַבָּר גדול</he>. Ker. l. c. <he>חוֹבֵר חֶבֶר דבלאו הדין הוא</he> but what kind of charmer (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 18:11">Deut. XVIII, 11</cite>) is he that is liable only to lashes (v. <cite ref="L00009"><he>לַאו</he></cite>)?; a. fr.—[

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 927:1">Yalk. Job 927</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Job 40:30">Job XL, 30</cite>) <he>מי שח׳ עצמו במצות</he> whoever befriended himself with good deeds; Tanḥ. Nitsab. 4 (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 14:2">Kel. XIV, 2</cite> <he>וחִבְּרָהּ לו</he> (or <he>וחֲבָרָהּ</he>) and he fastened the tube to it (the staff).

Ib. משיְחַבֵּר from the moment he attaches it, opp. משיחבל, v. חָבַל.—Part. pass. מְחוּבָּר. Ib. XII, 2 כל המ׳ וכ׳ whatever is fastened (belonging) to an object fit to become unclean &c.—מ׳ (לקרקע) fixed, immovable, opp. תלוש.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 89a:3">B. Mets. 89ᵃ</cite> <he>אוכל במ׳</he> may eat of what is standing in the field (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:25">Deut. XXIII, 25</cite>, sq.).

Peah IV, 1, v. דָּלִית. Y. ib. 18ᵃ ואינו מ׳ and when the Mishnah says בדלית ובדקל, it does not mean במ׳ בדלית וכ׳ ‘of that which is attached to the vine and tree’; אין תימר מ׳ הוא וכ׳ if you say, it means that which is attached, then the Mishnah means to say that the owner must designate the Peah while it is up (on the tree) &c.—Ib. II, beg. 16ᵈ (in a passage misplaced and corrupted) הא גדר מ׳ ואינו מ׳ this ‘fence’ (Mish. ib. II, 3) is to be considered as something attached to the ground (like a growth) and (in other respects) as not attached.

senses.gloss: to charm. Lam. R., introd. (R. Josh. 2) התחיל מְחַבֵּר חֲבָרִים (not מחבי חביים) he began to consult charmers (with ref. to Ez. XXI, 26).
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 65a:19">Snh. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>מקטר לחַבֵּר</he> he burns incense for charming purposes (to exorcise the demons); a. fr.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 80:2">Gen. R. s. 80</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Hosea 6:9">Hos. VI, 9</cite>) as the priests <he>נֶחְכָּרִים על וכ׳</he> are grooped around &c.; <cite ref="Makkot 10a:3">Macc. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>מִתְחַבְּרִין וכ׳</he>.
Num. R. s. 20, beg. נִתְחַבְּרוּ מואב וכ׳ Moab and Midian formed an alliance; Tanḥ. Balak 3.—3) to be charmed, spellbound.

<cite ref="Exodus 18">B’shall. 18</cite> <he>מיד נתח׳ וכ׳</he> at once the bird is spellbound (by the snake looking at its shadow) and falls to pieces; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 255">Yalk. Ex. 255</cite> <cite ref="M03002"><he>מת</he></cite> (read <he>מתחבר</he>); Mekh. B’shall., Vayassa, s. 1 <he>מִתְחַבֵּר על צלו</he> (not <he>ומת׳ אל</he>) it remains spell-bound over its own shadow.
